body.statement: In the balanced two-arm binary finite-population problem, the minimax risk of the reduced shifted-binomial experiment equals the minimax risk obtained by jointly optimizing over all schedule-independent assignment laws and all estimators; the reduced game has a unique minimax rule and a least-favorable-prior Bayes representation.

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 2.1. r_n*=ρ_n*=inf_f sup_{I_n} E(f(p+Bin(r,1/2))−(p−q)/n)². Moreover, there is a unique f_n* minimizing (6) and it is the posterior mean of (p−q)/n under a least-favorable prior π_n* on I_n. As a consequence, f_n* is admissible and ρ_n* is the Bayes risk of π_n*. Theorem 2.2. Let f_n* be the function minimizing (6) in the reduced model. Then inf_{A,τ̂} sup_{P∈{0,1}²ⁿ} R_n(A,τ̂)=ρ_n*.
